title: F. Yet Another Problem About Pairs Satisfying an Inequality
statement:
You are given an array a_1, a_2, … a_n. Count the number of pairs of indices 1 ≤ i, j ≤ n such that a_i < i < a_j < j.

The first line contains an integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 1000) — the number of test cases.

The first line of each test case contains an integer n (2 ≤ n ≤ 2·10^5) — the length of the array.

The second line of each test case contains n integers a_1, a_2, …, a_n (0 ≤ a_i ≤ 10^9) — the elements of the array.

It is guaranteed that the sum of n across all test cases does not exceed 2·10^5.

For each test case, output a single integer — the number of pairs of indices satisfying the condition in the statement.

Please note, that the answer for some test cases won't fit into 32-bit integer type, so you should use at least 64-bit integer type in your programming language (like long long for C++).

For the first test cases the pairs are (i, j) = {(2, 4), (2, 8), (3, 8)}.

Input:
```
581 1 2 3 8 2 1 421 2100 2 1 6 3 4 1 2 8 321 100000000030 1000000000 2
```

Output:
```
3
0
10
0
1
```
